name: European Badger
description: The European badger is a powerfully built black, white, and grey animal with a small head, stocky body, small black eyes, and short tail. They live in family groups (called cete/clan) in a series of underground tunnels called a sett. They help control pest populations.
habitat: Woodlands, hedgerows, and grasslands across the UK
diet: Omnivore - earthworms, insects, fruits, cereals, and small mammals
funFact: Badgers are incredibly clean animals and have separate toilet areas away from their setts!
conservation: Least Concern - Protected under the Protection of Badgers Act 1992
tips: Leave a shallow dish of water in your garden

name: European Hedgehog
description: The European hedgehog is a spiny mammal native to Europe. They feed on insects.They are nocturnal animals that hibernate during winter. Their spines are actually modified hairs made of keratin.
diet: Insectivore - beetles, caterpillars, earthworms, and slugs
conservation: Vulnerable - UK population has declined by 50% since 2000
funFact: A hedgehog has around 5,000 to 7,000 spines on its back!
tips: Make a hedgehog highway (small gaps in fences)
Leave piles of leaves for hibernation

name: Eurasian Otter
description: The Eurasian otter is a semiaquatic mammal with a sleek body, webbed feet, and a powerful tail. Once nearly extinct in Britain, their numbers have recovered significantly.
habitat: Rivers, lakes, coastal areas, and wetlands
diet: Carnivore - fish, crustaceans, amphibians, and water birds
conservation: Near Threatened - Now found in every county in England
funFact: Otters can close their ears and nostrils when swimming underwater!
tips: Keep rivers clean – don't litter near water
Report oil spills if you see them

name: Red Fox
description: The red fox is the largest of the true foxes and one of the most widely distributed members of the Carnivora, found across the entire Northern Hemisphere. They are highly adaptable and can live in a variety of habitats.
habitat: Forests, grasslands, mountains, deserts, and urban areas
diet: Omnivore (opportunistic) - rabbits, rodents, birds, insects, fruits, and vegetables
funFact: Foxes have super-hearing, they can hear a watch ticking from 40 yards away!
tips: Secure your bins so foxes don't scatter rubbish
Enjoy watching them from a distance
conservation: Least Concern - population stable throughout the UK

name: Red Deer
description: The red deer is one of the largest deer species and UK largest mammal. A male red deer is called a stag or hart, and a female is called a doe or hind
funFact: Red deer are the national animal of Scotland and Wales
conservation: Least Concern - UK population has increased by 50% since 2000
tips: Drive carefully on rural roads at dawn/dusk
Plant native trees to provide food

name: Red Squirrel
description: small, agile woodland mammals known for their reddish-brown fur, bushy tail, and distinctive large ear tufts. Not to be confused with: the grey squirrel which is native to the United States.
Diet: nuts, seeds, tree shoots and other plant matter
funFact: Red squirrels can jump more than 2m – not bad for an animal with a body length of less than 25cm!
conservation: Endangered - in England and wales and near threatened in Scotland due to competition and disease from invasive grey squirrels
tips: Put up bird feeders that squirrels can't reach
Plant bulb flowers they don't dig up
